findings.summary: Core browser sign-in uses ephemeral http://127.0.0.1 loopback, ~43-character state, and mandatory PKCE. WHOOP documents https or whoop:// redirects, an eight-character state, and no PKCE. Compatibility is unproven; live app access is missing.
findings.evidence: packages/core/src/auth/loopback.ts port 0; packages/core/src/auth/oauth.ts STATE_BYTES=32; WHOOP OAuth page 2026-09-06
findings.invariant: Reuse Core OAuth without weakening CSRF/PKCE

findings.summary: A hosted HTTPS callback would match WHOOP's documented redirect form and secret-custody rule but is a hosted service. RFC 0000 §3 and this packet forbid implementing a broker.
WHOOP refresh sample includes scope=offline; Core refreshTokens does not post scope. Live requirement unknown.
go-no-go whoop evidence is live-account. No WHOOP membership, dashboard app, or tokens exist here. Status UNRESOLVED, not PASS.
